prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station (start permissives; lost permissive→alarm/stop; maintenance release after isolations tagged/verified/logged). Lantern=SCADA Historian Server (critical; trends/doses/analyzers/filters/washes/lab times; uses Sample Chain Slip; retains data for reconstruction/compliance). Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid (sends Alum Batch Ticket; receives Jar Test Photograph Set; holds last approved dose on bad data). Cobalt=North Filter Gallery (staggers washes). Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (sends Jar Test Photograph Set; logs distribution samples). Quarry=Maintenance Planner (weekly account review; receives Clearwell Diver Entry Permit to verify isolation before confined-space release; receives Rake Torque Snapshot). Juniper=High Service Pump Header (produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; lead/lag). Falcon=Distribution Dispatcher (sends Pressure Zone Handoff Card; notified before changes and of Juniper/North/South Distribution Pressure Station failures affecting pressure zones/fire flow; radio/phone field coordination). Elements: Raw Water Screen Channel (Rake Torque Snapshot→Maintenance Planner); South Filter Gallery (Filter Run Exception Note→Chief Operator); Clearwell Level Controller (sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit); Chlorine Contact Basin; Backwash Recovery Tank; North/South Distribution Pressure Stations (comms loss→last mode); workstations; controllers; backup generator, ATS, UPS. Actors: Chief Operator (Backwash Solids Manifest; alarm governance; directs emergency priorities; requires post-event review: cause/services/corrective actions/procedure changes), Duty Engineer (receives Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before chlorine storage change; authorizes logged, bounded temporary workarounds; confirms pre-wet-commissioning staff understanding), Laboratory Technician (Sample Chain Slip; lab accounts no control actions), Chemical Supplier Driver (Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log), Field crews. Item: Chlorine Residual Alarm (high priority). Requirements: RBAC named accounts, no shared credentials; least privilege; remote access MFA+encryption+approval; segmentation; patches tested; alarm priority by consequence; shelving controlled; backup power for intake, screen, contact basin, clearwell, historian, HSP header, control room; written generator/ATS/fuel expectations; UPS bridges transfer, orderly shutdown; reliability: sensor-failure detection, redundant

Document units:
S229: Functional testing shall verify that the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, and Coagulant Dosing Skid respond correctly to local and supervisory commands.
S230: During integrated testing, Juniper shall demonstrate stable pressure control through startup, lead-lag transfer, and controlled shutdown.
S231: The SCADA Historian Server shall be checked for correct time synchronization, tag naming, data retention, and retrieval of key commissioning trends.
S232: The Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller shall be tested under representative level, flow, and residual control conditions before treated water is released for routine distribution.
S233: Storm Intake Mode shall be exercised in a planned drill that confirms operator prompts, intake constraints, and return-to-normal steps.
S234: A Chlorine Residual Alarm test shall verify annunciation, operator response guidance, acknowledgement behavior, and escalation to the appropriate duty staff.
S235: The Chief Operator shall coordinate training so that operators understand the control concept, normal sequencing, manual fallback methods, and alarm response expectations.
S236: Operator training shall include classroom review, simulator or dry-run practice where practical, field walkdowns, and supervised operation during early service.
S237: The Laboratory Technician shall be trained on sample timing, result entry, data review responsibilities, and communication of unusual water quality findings.
S238: The Maintenance Planner shall review commissioning defects, recurring nuisance alarms, calibration drift, and equipment access problems before preventive maintenance intervals are finalized.
S239: The Maintenance Planner shall use the clip to compare observed pump condition with planned inspection intervals and corrective work priorities.
S240: Feedback from maintenance work orders shall be reviewed with operations so that control changes do not mask equipment degradation or create avoidable field effort.
S241: Distribution readiness shall be declared only after pressure control, reservoir or clearwell constraints, communications, and emergency contact paths have been verified.
S242: Falcon shall confirm that distribution readiness messages are acknowledged before any planned change in pressure zone operating status.
S243: Before distribution readiness is declared, the South Distribution Pressure Station shall use the card to confirm zone status, valve lineup, and communication checks.
S244: The North Distribution Pressure Station shall be included in readiness checks for telemetry validity, pump permissives, local alarm indication, and operator communications.
S245: During commissioning of residuals handling, the Residuals Hauler shall use the Backwash Solids Manifest to confirm load identity, destination, and acceptance requirements.
